question: The main purpose of tracheobronchial suctioning is to remove secretions and maintain what?
explanation: Removing mucus from the lower respiratory tract keeps the airway open and clear for breathing. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is suction applied intermittently instead of continuously during the procedure?
explanation: Continuous suction pulls hard on the delicate lining of the airway and causes physical injury. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h1)

question: Which clinical sign is a clear indication for performing tracheobronchial suctioning?
explanation: The presence of mucus blocking the artificial tube signals an immediate need for clearing. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which of the following conditions is NOT a safe reason to perform routine suctioning?

options.A: The patient has coarse breath sounds
options.D: Secretions are visible in the tube

explanation: Suctioning should only be done based on clinical need, never just as a routine task or schedule convenience. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h2)

question: What is the recommended suction pressure range for an adult patient?
explanation: Adult airways tolerate this pressure range safely without excessive trauma or collapse. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h3)

question: Why must sterile gloves be worn during the insertion of the suction catheter?

options.A: To protect the nurse from catching a cold
options.B: To prevent introducing bacteria into the lungs
options.C: To keep the nurse's hands from getting wet
options.D: To prevent the catheter from slipping

explanation: The lower respiratory tract is sterile, so sterile technique stops outside pathogens from causing pneumonia. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h3)

question: What mandatory step must be performed right before suctioning to prevent low oxygen levels?
explanation: Giving extra oxygen beforehand builds a safety buffer against the hypoxia caused by vacuuming air out. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h4)

question: A patient with an endotracheal tube shows an oxygen saturation drop during preparation. What should the nurse do first?
explanation: Suctioning an already hypoxic patient worsens their condition, so oxygen must be restored first. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended time for a single suction pass?
explanation: Limiting suction time prevents dangerous oxygen depletion and cardiac stress in the patient. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why should the suction catheter be rotated during withdrawal?

options.A: To remove secretions evenly from all sides
options.B: To prevent the catheter from coiling up
options.C: To cool down the plastic material
options.D: To speed up the removal of the tube

explanation: Rotating the catheter prevents it from pulling continuously on just one part of the mucosal wall. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which heart rhythm disturbance can be triggered by vagal nerve stimulation during airway suctioning?
explanation: Irritation of the vagus nerve in the airway can disturb the normal electrical rhythm of the heart. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h6)

question: A patient becomes bradycardic and cyanotic midway through suctioning. What is the immediate nursing action?

options.B: Turn off the wall monitor and document the event
options.C: Call the surgeon to inspect the tracheostomy site
options.D: Push the catheter deeper to clear remaining mucus

explanation: Bradycardia and cyanosis indicate severe oxygen deprivation, requiring immediate cessation and rescue ventilation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h6)

question: What physical finding best indicates that the suctioning procedure was effective?
explanation: Clearing mucus from the airways restores normal airflow and reduces noisy rhonchi or crackles. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which detail is most important to include in the nursing documentation after suctioning?

options.A: Cost of the sterile gloves used
options.B: Exact manufacturer of the wall regulator
options.C: Brand name of the suction catheter

explanation: Documenting secretion characteristics helps the medical team track respiratory infections and recovery progress. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h7)
